key_insight: A 2k-dimensional Euclidean space (R^{2k}) is theoretically sufficient — and in many formulations tight — to represent subset membership for top-k retrieval, so embedding-based top-k decisions need far lower dimension than the combinatorial number of subsets suggests.
problem_solved: Determines the minimal embedding dimension required to encode membership of up to k-item subsets from m items (the Minimal Embeddable Dimension, MED), resolving how compactly one can represent exponentially many subsets for top-k retrieval.
method: Formally define MED for m items and all subsets of size ≤ k and derive information-theoretic lower bounds.
Construct explicit embedding schemes and matching upper bounds showing R^{2k} suffices under ℓ2, inner-product, and cosine similarity notions.
Empirically validate theoretical claims with simulations in practical settings (finite m, noisy/approximate distances) to confirm achievability.
impact: Provides a principled guideline to set embedding dimensionality for top-k retrieval systems — enabling much smaller, more efficient representations without sacrificing exactness under common similarity measures.
visual_elements: Schematic: items and k-subsets mapped into a 2k-dimensional vector space (arrow from combinatorial set to compact vector representation).
Plot: MED (required dimension) vs. k showing the 2k line and comparisons to naive combinatorial complexity.
Table/heatmap: comparison of tight bounds and empirical error across similarity measures (ℓ2, inner product, cosine).
Pipeline diagram: embedding construction → similarity scoring → top-k retrieval, annotated with storage/compute savings.
paper_title: $\mathbb{R}^{2k}$ is Theoretically Large Enough for Embedding-based Top-$k$ Retrieval
paper_authors: Zihao Wang, Hang Yin, Lihui Liu, Hanghang Tong, Yangqiu Song
